data.最后完整循环的选取#最后完整循环的选取:

若最后一个循环完整（正、负扫均有数据），则直接使用。 若最后一个循环不完整（仅含单向扫描），则回退至倒数第二个循环。

本 Workflow 用于处理辰华电化学工作站导出的原始文本格式（.txt）CV 数据。通过自动识别测试参数，将连续的测试曲线拆分为独立的循环，并根据扫描方向（正向/负向）对数据进行精确对齐和配对，最终导出为结构化的 Excel 表格。
本 Workflow 是所有后续 CV 分析流程的数据基础。
data.cv-扫描分段原理#CV 扫描分段原理:
循环伏安法通过在工作电极上施加三角波电位扫描来表征电化学行为。一个完整的循环（Cycle）通常包含两个扫描段（Segment）：
正向扫描（Forward Scan）：电位向正方向增加，对应阳极过程。 负向扫描（Reverse Scan）：电位向负方向减小，对应阴极过程。
data.full_cycles完整循环#Full_Cycles（完整循环）: 将数据按完整圈数排列，每一圈包含完整的正扫和负扫。用于绘制多圈重叠的 CV 曲线，观察循环稳定性。
data.metadata元数据#Metadata（元数据）:
记录该样品的原始测试条件，包括：
参数 含义 单位 init_e 初始电位 V high_e / low_e 电位窗口上/下限 V scan_rate 扫描速率 V/s sample_interval 采样间隔 V
data.scans_split分段扫描#Scans_Split（分段扫描）: 将正向扫描与负向扫描彻底分离，格式为 C{n}_forward 和 C{n}_reverse。该页签是后续 CV: 计算库伦效率、CV/赝电容分析: 取中点电流值分别计算正负扫、CV/Cdl 等分析流程的核心输入数据。
data.常见问题#常见问题: 科学计数法：系统可自动识别 1.0e-03 等科学计数法格式的电流值。 不完整循环：若某次循环未完成（仅包含单向扫描），系统将保留该段数据并标记，不影响其余循环的正常处理。
data.循环拆分#循环拆分:
通过检测电位序列的极值点（Turning Points）来识别扫描方向的切换。当电位 EiE_iEi​ 满足以下条件时，该点被判定为转折点：
Ei≈Ehigh 或 Ei≈Elow,(Ei−Ei−1)⋅(Ei+1−Ei)≤0E_i \approx E_{\text{high}} \;\text{或}\; E_i \approx E_{\text{low}}, \quad (E_i - E_{i-1}) \cdot (E_{i+1} - E_i) \leq 0Ei​≈Ehigh​或Ei​≈Elow​,(Ei​−Ei−1​)⋅(Ei+1​−Ei​)≤0端点补全（Endpoint Completion）：由于硬件采样频率限制，实际记录的最后一个数据点可能未完全到达设定的 EhighE_{\text{high}}Ehigh​ 或 ElowE_{\text{low}}Elow​。系统将自动进行数学插值补全，确保每个扫描段都位于严格定义的电位窗口 [Elow, Ehigh][E_{\text{low}},\, E_{\text{high}}][Elow​,Ehigh​] 内，从而消除后续积分计算因窗口不一致导致的系统误差。
data.操作步骤#操作步骤: 选择输入文件夹：在文件选择器中选择存放电化学工作站导出的 .txt 原始数据文件的文件夹。 自动处理完成后，输出文件夹将在界面中显示，可直接点击打开。 同时会自动绘制各扫速下最后一圈 CV 曲线的叠加图，用于快速预览数据质量。
data.数据对齐与闭合#数据对齐与闭合:
为保证曲线的连续性，系统实现了跨扫描对齐：
确保前一个扫描段的终点与后一个扫描段的起点在物理空间上重合。 在完整循环（Full Cycles）模式下，强制数据以最低电位起始并闭合，以便直接用于绘图或积分计算。

应该选择一个文件夹，这个文件夹里有如果扫速原始数据文件。其中每个原始数据文件的类似为：

如果你已经看过 Nyquist/Bode，但还想搞明白“到底是哪一段动力学在主导响应”，这个 Workflow 就是为这个问题准备的。
它会对提取后的 EIS 数据执行 DRT（Distribution of Relaxation Times）分析，把频域阻抗信息映射到时间常数分布上，帮助你更直观地区分不同过程（如界面电荷转移、扩散相关过程等）。

每个样品会输出以下数据文件：
fit_data.csv：实验阻抗、DRT 重建阻抗及残差 drt_data.csv：τ\tauτ 与 γ(τ)\gamma(\tau)γ(τ) 分布 summary.json：正则化参数与求解摘要（如 lambda_value、epsilon） 并输出以下图像：
nyquist_fit.png：实验与 DRT 拟合 Nyquist 对比 drt_tau.png：γ\gammaγ–τ\tauτ 分布图（横轴对数） residuals.png：实部/虚部残差图 *_drt_plots.opju：Origin 工程（同样包含 Nyquist、DRT 与残差图）

data.原理简要#原理（简要）:
DRT 将阻抗表示为不同时间常数过程的叠加，核心思想可写为：
Z(ω)=R∞+∫γ(τ)1+jωτ dln⁡τZ(\omega)=R_\infty + \int \frac{\gamma(\tau)}{1+j\omega\tau} \, d\ln\tauZ(ω)=R∞​+∫1+jωτγ(τ)​dlnτ其中：
γ(τ)\gamma(\tau)γ(τ) 的峰位反映特征过程对应的时间尺度 峰面积/高度与该过程贡献强弱相关 这比仅看 Nyquist 半圆更容易分辨“多个机制叠加”的情况。
data.实用建议#实用建议: 如果你是第一次做 DRT，建议先用 EIS 绘图：Nyquist 和 Bode 快速检查曲线是否平滑、是否存在明显异常点，再进入本步骤，通常能得到更稳定、更可解释的结果。

This Workflow uses the output data from Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to calculate the charge quantities for forward and reverse scans in each cycle through numerical integration, thereby obtaining coulombic efficiency and electrode capacitance.
data.capacitance-calculation#Capacitance Calc:
For electrode materials with capacitive characteristics, capacitance CCC is defined as the ratio of charge to the potential window ΔE\Delta EΔE:
C=QΔE=∫∣I∣ dtEhigh−ElowC = \frac{Q}{\Delta E} = \frac{\int |I|\, \mathrm{d}t}{E_{\text{high}} - E_{\text{low}}}C=ΔEQ​=Ehigh​−Elow​∫∣I∣dt​where EhighE_{\text{high}}Ehigh​ and ElowE_{\text{low}}Elow​ are the upper and lower limits of the scan potential window, respectively.
data.charge-calculation#Charge Calculation:
By definition of electric current, the charge QQQ is the integral of current III over time ttt. For discrete data, numerical integration is performed using the Trapezoidal Rule:
Q=∫t1t2I(t) dt≈∑k=1N−1I(tk)+I(tk+1)2⋅ΔtQ = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} I(t)\, \mathrm{d}t \approx \sum_{k=1}^{N-1} \frac{I(t_k) + I(t_{k+1})}{2} \cdot \Delta tQ=∫t1​t2​​I(t)dt≈k=1∑N−1​2I(tk​)+I(tk+1​)​⋅Δtwhere the time step Δt\Delta tΔt is derived from the sampling interval and scan rate:
Δt=ΔEsampleν\Delta t = \frac{\Delta E_{\text{sample}}}{\nu}Δt=νΔEsample​​Here ΔEsample\Delta E_{\text{sample}}ΔEsample​ is the sampling voltage interval (V) and ν\nuν is the scan rate (V/s).
data.coulombic-efficiency#Coulombic Efficienc:
Coulombic Efficiency (CE) is defined as the ratio of charge from the reverse scan (reduction process) to the forward scan (oxidation process):
ηCE=QreverseQforward×100%\eta_{\text{CE}} = \frac{Q_{\text{reverse}}}{Q_{\text{forward}}} \times 100\%ηCE​=Qforward​Qreverse​​×100%This metric reflects the degree of reversibility of the electrode process. For an ideal fully reversible process, coulombic efficiency should approach 100%.

Contains detailed calculation results for each cycle in each file:
Field Meaning Q_Forward / Q_Reverse Forward/reverse scan charge (C) CE (%) Coulombic efficiency Cap_Forward / Cap_Reverse Forward/reverse scan capacitance (F) Cap_Avg Average capacitance (F)

This Workflow processes raw text format (.txt) CV data exported from CHI electrochemical workstations. It automatically identifies test parameters, splits continuous test curves into independent cycles, precisely aligns and pairs data according to scan direction (forward/reverse), and exports the results as structured Excel spreadsheets.
This Workflow serves as the data foundation for all subsequent CV analysis processes.
data.cv-scan-segmentation-principle#CV Scan S:
Cyclic voltammetry characterizes electrochemical behavior by applying a triangular wave potential scan to the working electrode. A complete cycle typically consists of two scan segments:
Forward Scan: Potential increases in the positive direction, corresponding to the anodic process. Reverse Scan: Potential decreases in the negative direction, corresponding to the cathodic process.
data.cycle-splitting#Cycle Splitting:
Scan direction switching is identified by detecting turning points in the potential sequence. A point is identified as a turning point when the potential EiE_iEi​ satisfies the following conditions:
Ei≈Ehigh or Ei≈Elow,(Ei−Ei−1)⋅(Ei+1−Ei)≤0E_i \approx E_{\text{high}} \;\text{or}\; E_i \approx E_{\text{low}}, \quad (E_i - E_{i-1}) \cdot (E_{i+1} - E_i) \leq 0Ei​≈Ehigh​orEi​≈Elow​,(Ei​−Ei−1​)⋅(Ei+1​−Ei​)≤0Endpoint Completion: Due to hardware sampling frequency limitations, the last recorded data point may not fully reach the set EhighE_{\text{high}}Ehigh​ or ElowE_{\text{low}}Elow​. data.cv-scan-segmentation-principle#CV Scan S:
Cyclic voltammetry characterizes electrochemical behavior by applying a triangular wave potential scan to the working electrode. A complete cycle typically consists of two scan segments:
Forward Scan: Potential increases in the positive direction, corresponding to oxidation reactions. Reverse Scan: Potential decreases in the negative direction, corresponding to reduction reactions.

This Workflow uses the output data from Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to determine the double-layer capacitance CdlC_{\text{dl}}Cdl​ by linear fitting of the difference between anodic and cathodic currents at the mid-point potential across different scan rates. This can be further used to calculate the Electrochemically Active Surface Area (ECSA).
Prerequisites First execute Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing or Cyclic Voltammetry (CV) Data Extraction and Preprocessing to complete CV data extraction. The input folder should contain CV extraction results at multiple different scan rates.

The charging current ici_cic​ is proportional to the scan rate ν\nuν:

If you’ve already looked at Nyquist/Bode plots but still want to understand “which kinetic process is actually dominating the response,” this Workflow is designed for that question.
It performs DRT (Distribution of Relaxation Times) analysis on the extracted EIS data, mapping frequency-domain impedance information to a time constant distribution, helping you more intuitively distinguish different processes (such as interfacial charge transfer, diffusion-related processes, etc.).
data.analysis-and-fitting-results#Analysis an:
Each sample produces the following data files:
fit_data.csv: Experimental impedance, DRT-reconstructed impedance, and residuals drt_data.csv: τ\tauτ and γ(τ)\gamma(\tau)γ(τ) distribution summary.json: Regularization parameters and solution summary (e.g., lambda_value, epsilon) And the following plots:
nyquist_fit.png: Experimental vs. DRT-fitted Nyquist comparison drt_tau.png: γ\gammaγ–τ\tauτ distribution plot (logarithmic x-axis) residuals.png: Real/imaginary part residual plot *_drt_plots.opju: Origin project (also containing Nyquist, DRT, and residual plots)
data.faq#FAQ: Why are some samples missing results? Common reasons include missing input columns or data containing invalid values; the program will skip and report the specific error.
data.practical-tips#Practical Tips: If this is your first time doing DRT, it’s recommended to first use EIS Plotting: Nyquist and Bode Visualization to quickly check whether curves are smooth and whether there are obvious outliers, then proceed to this step. This usually yields more stable and more interpretable results.

data.principle-brief#Principle (Brief):
DRT represents impedance as a superposition of processes with different time constants. The core idea can be written as:
Z(ω)=R∞+∫γ(τ)1+jωτ dln⁡τZ(\omega)=R_\infty + \int \frac{\gamma(\tau)}{1+j\omega\tau} \, d\ln\tauZ(ω)=R∞​+∫1+jωτγ(τ)​dlnτwhere:
The peak positions of γ(τ)\gamma(\tau)γ(τ) reflect the characteristic time scales of the corresponding processes Peak area/height is related to the contribution strength of that process This makes it easier to resolve “multiple mechanisms superimposed” compared to just looking at Nyquist semicircles.
